text:
Maya: CI nightly flagged a perf regression on H100 for long-chat workloads, attaching initial profile.
Nikhil: can you paste the flame/trace link and a quick delta? how big is the regression?
Maya: flame here: https://ci.internal/perf/1719876543/flame.svg — p50 tokens/sec down ~12% on H100 at seq=1024, p95 latency up ~20ms
Kai: my gut: kernel selector falling back to a conservative GEMM path when KV-frag / batchshape distribution changes. saw selector decisions in logs.
Maya: snippet from runtime log:
```
[2026-04-01T02:12:34Z] kernel_selector: model=rwkv-1.2, seq=1024, chosen_kernel=gemm_warp_v1, score=47.3, fallback_reason=kv_fragmentation
[2026-04-01T02:12:34Z] batch_formation: window_ms=8, max_tokens_per_batch=24576, packed_tokens=18340, kv_frag=0.32
```
Sara: interesting — on A10 we saw the opposite: windowing increased (more small slices) after recent continuous-batching tweak, which hurt packing efficiency and bumped kernel mismatches.
Devon: proposal: run a focused sweep that adjusts two knobs per card family: (1) max_tokens_per_batch, (2) packing_window_safety_margin (how aggressively we close the window early to avoid KV frag). run AB vs current.
Devon: suggested starting values (conservative, measurable):
- A10: max_tokens_per_batch=15360 -> 18432 (+20%), safety_margin=0.15 -> 0.10
- T4: max_tokens_per_batch=8192 -> 10000 (+22%), safety_margin=0.18 -> 0.12
- L4: max_tokens_per_batch=10240 -> 12288 (+20%), safety_margin=0.16 -> 0.11
- A100: max_tokens_per_batch=24576 -> 28672 (+17%), safety_margin=0.14 -> 0.10
- H100: max_tokens_per_batch=32768 -> 32768 (no change initially), safety_margin=0.13 -> 0.11
Maya: rationale: increase headroom so kernel selector more often picks the high-throughput kernels (fewer fallbacks) while slightly loosening the safety margin on cheaper cards to improve packing. H100 unchanged to validate cause vs regression.
Nikhil: test matrix: synthetic traffic (low/med/high entropy), real chat replay (top 100 customers), and kernel microbench. Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, KV hit ratio, kernel_fallback_rate, error rate.
Sara: also add a control where we reduce continuous-batching max_wait_ms for interactive routes from 8ms -> 5ms to see latency tradeoff vs packing. Might reduce opportunity for large packs but helps p95.
Kai: add kernel-hinting flag in runtime for experiment: prefer_matmul_opt=true for packs with packed_tokens > threshold. quick patch:
```
if (packed_tokens > 16000) { selector.hint = "prefer_fast_matmul"; }
```
Maya: good. opsbot, can you create canary rollout for these configs and tag experiment id cb-safety-2026-04-01?
opsbot: Created canary rollout cb-safety-2026-04-01 -> cluster: canary-rt-3, targeting 5% infra. Configs pushed to /cfg/experiments/cb-safety-2026-04-01.json
Kai: if KV-frag persists we should instrument per-prefix KV hit scatter and consider prefix-level caching to reduce fragmentation before touching kernels.
Sara: I'll run kernel microbench per-card today and upload numbers to the experiment doc (ETA EOD PST).
Devon: I'll prepare the AB analysis script to compute kernel_fallback_rate and per-kernel tokens/sec. will hook it to perf dashboard.
Maya: thanks all — we'll reconvene tomorrow with initial metrics. :thumbsup:
